newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat falls sharply on rain in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat falls sharply on rain in Kansas.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures fell sharply in early trade and the September contract was down more than half the 20-cent per bushel daily limit after rains fell in Kansas over the weekend, traders said.
The moisture improved crop prospects in dry areas of Kansas, typically the leading U.S. hard red winter wheat producing state, traders said.
Traders said Produce Grain and LIT each sold two million bushels July in early trade while Cargill Investor Services and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp each sold one million July.
At 0958 CDT, wheat was down 10-1/2 to six cents per bushel with July off eight at $3.67.
